{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My capacity for forgiveness was praised by everyone who knew me. I forgave my husband's first affair, then his second, then his financial deceptions. Friends admired my 'grace.' By the time I realized forgiveness without boundaries is just permission, I'd lost a decade and my retirement savings.

CANDIDATE A:
My capacity for forgiveness was praised by everyone who knew me. When my husband had his first affair, I forgave him after he showed genuine remorse. When financial deceptions came to light, I set boundaries instead of simply forgiving again. Friends noticed I'd learned to balance grace with self-protection. My strength became knowing when forgiveness was appropriate and when it wasn't.

CANDIDATE B:
My curiosity made me a great journalist—I asked questions others wouldn't. Then I couldn't stop. I investigated friends' marriages, my children's private lives, my neighbors' finances. My need to know destroyed every relationship I had. The trait that built my career dismantled my personal life.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:56"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both the SITUATION and CANDIDATE A involve a journey of personal growth where initial forgiveness leads to the realization of the need for boundaries, contrasting with the admiration of others."}
